parse_failures_summary.note: The 5s deadline is wall-clock per file, so the outcome depends on machine load: 19 of the 43 parse in 2.5-5.05s when alone and failed only because 4 workers ran concurrently; 24 fail even alone. Failed files contribute zero symbols and zero references (regex estimate: about 601 library methods + 2,282 test methods in the 43 files).

definitions.standard: correct = right name at the right line with a kind in the right family (type vs callable). Enum members, fields and static readonly fields were NOT counted as expected (18 enum members and 26 fields in these files are also absent). 8 of the 38 correct rows carry a coarser kind: struct->class (2), enum->class (2), constructor->method (4).

spurious_return_type_methods.what: every method whose return type is a plain identifier also yields a second 'method' symbol named after the RETURN TYPE at the same line/col, e.g. method 'IXmlNode' at Converters/XmlNodeConverter.cs:57 (really CreateComment), method 'T' at Converters/CustomCreationConverter.cs:82, five methods named 'PathFilter' in Linq/JsonPath/JPath.cs. Not present in the 5 sampled files (their return types are predefined/nullable), so the sample's 100% precision overstates the index: index-wide method precision is at most 4382/4928 = 88.9%.

silent_loss_in_ok_files.what: Files with status 'ok' can lose most of their definitions. Linq/JContainer.cs (42.5KB, #if blocks inside the class base list and bodies) is 'ok' with 14 symbols: the class JContainer itself is absent and every member after line 360 is gone (InsertItem, RemoveItemAt, GetItem, SetItem, Add, Merge...; regex finds 46 method declarations, 13 extracted).

precision.standard: strict = exactly the declaration the C# compiler binds (static type's most-derived visible override, right overload). lenient = strict OR same virtual/interface slot (base declaration, or an override in some subtype of the receiver's static type) with a compatible overload.
